en: What keeps us healthy and happy
zh: 究竟是什么让我们一生都保持健康和幸福？

en: as we go through life?
zh: 在人生一路走来的过程中？

en: If you were going to invest now
zh: 假如现在要为未来的自己投资，

en: in your future best self,
zh: 让自己成为最好的样子，

en: where would you put your time and your energy?
zh: 你会把时间和精力投入到哪里？

en: There was a recent survey of millennials
zh: 最近有一项针对千禧一代的调查，

en: asking them what their most important life goals were,
zh: 询问他们人生中最重要的目标是什么，

en: and over 80 percent said
zh: 超过80%的人表示，

en: that a major life goal for them was to get rich.
zh: 他们的一项重要人生目标是变得富有。

en: And another 50 percent of those same young adults
zh: 而在同一批年轻人中，还有50%的人

en: said that another major life goal
zh: 表示他们的另一项重要人生目标

en: was to become famous.
zh: 是成名。

en: And we're constantly told to lean in to work, to push harder
zh: 我们也不断被告知，要全身心投入工作，要更加努力，

en: and achieve more.
zh: 取得更多成就。

en: We're given the impression that these are the things that we need to go after
zh: 我们得到的印象是，只有追求这些东西，

en: in order to have a good life.
zh: 才能过上美好的人生。

en: Pictures of entire lives,
zh: 想要完整地了解一个人的一生，

en: of the choices that people make and how those choices work out for them,
zh: 了解人们做出的选择，以及这些选择最终带来了什么结果，

en: those pictures are almost impossible to get.
zh: 几乎是不可能的。

en: Most of what we know about human life
zh: 我们对人生的大部分认识，

en: we know from asking people to remember the past,
zh: 都来自让人们回忆过去，

en: and as we know, hindsight is anything but 20/20.
zh: 而我们都知道，事后回想远没有想象中那么清晰准确。

en: We forget vast amounts of what happens to us in life,
zh: 我们会忘记人生中发生过的大量事情，

en: and sometimes memory is downright creative.
zh: 有时候，记忆甚至会自行编造情节。

en: But what if we could watch entire lives
zh: 但假如我们能够观察一个人的完整一生，

en: as they unfold through time?
zh: 看着它随着时间逐步展开呢？

en: What if we could study people from the time that they were teenagers
zh: 假如我们能从一个人的青少年时期开始研究，

en: all the way into old age
zh: 一直追踪到他们步入老年，

en: to see what really keeps people happy and healthy?
zh: 看看究竟是什么让人保持幸福和健康呢？

en: We did that.
zh: 我们真的这样做了。

en: The Harvard Study of Adult Development
zh: 哈佛大学成人发展研究

en: may be the longest study of adult life that's ever been done.
zh: 可能是有史以来持续时间最长的成人生活研究。

en: For 75 years, we've tracked the lives of 724 men,
zh: 75年来，我们一直追踪724名男性的人生，

en: year after year, asking about their work, their home lives, their health,
zh: 年复一年地询问他们的工作、家庭生活和健康状况，

en: and of course asking all along the way without knowing how their life stories
zh: 当然，在整个过程中，我们并不知道他们的人生故事

en: were going to turn out.
zh: 最终会走向何方。

en: Studies like this are exceedingly rare.
zh: 这样的研究极其罕见。

en: Almost all projects of this kind fall apart within a decade
zh: 几乎所有此类研究项目都会在十年内中断，

en: because too many people drop out of the study,
zh: 因为有太多参与者退出研究，

en: or funding for the research dries up,
zh: 或者研究经费枯竭，

en: or the researchers get distracted,
zh: 或者研究人员转移了注意力，

en: or they die, and nobody moves the ball further down the field.
zh: 又或者他们去世了，之后再也没人把研究继续推进下去。

en: But through a combination of luck
zh: 但凭借一些运气，

en: and the persistence of several generations of researchers,
zh: 以及几代研究人员坚持不懈的努力，

en: this study has survived.
zh: 这项研究一直延续到了今天。

en: About 60 of our original 724 men
zh: 最初的724名男性中，大约还有60人

en: are still alive,
zh: 依然健在，

en: still participating in the study,
zh: 也仍然在参与这项研究，

en: most of them in their 90s.
zh: 他们大多已经九十多岁了。

en: And we are now beginning to study
zh: 现在，我们也开始研究

en: the more than 2,000 children of these men.
zh: 这些男性的两千多名子女。

en: And I'm the fourth director of the study.
zh: 而我是这项研究的第四任负责人。

en: Since 1938, we've tracked the lives of two groups of men.
zh: 从1938年开始，我们一直追踪两组男性的人生。

en: The first group started in the study
zh: 第一组人在加入研究时，

en: when they were sophomores at Harvard College.
zh: 还是哈佛学院的大学二年级学生。

en: They all finished college during World War II,
zh: 他们都在第二次世界大战期间完成了大学学业，

en: and then most went off to serve in the war.
zh: 随后大多数人都奔赴战场服役。

en: And the second group that we've followed
zh: 我们追踪的第二组人，

en: was a group of boys from Boston's poorest neighborhoods,
zh: 是来自Boston最贫困社区的一群男孩，

en: boys who were chosen for the study
zh: 之所以选择这些男孩参与研究，

en: specifically because they were from some of the most troubled
zh: 正是因为他们来自当时处境最艰难、

en: and disadvantaged families
zh: 条件最不利的一些家庭，

en: in the Boston of the 1930s.
zh: 生活在20世纪30年代的Boston。

en: Most lived in tenements, many without hot and cold running water.
zh: 他们大多住在廉租公寓里，许多人家里甚至没有冷热自来水。

en: When they entered the study,
zh: 刚加入研究时，

en: all of these teenagers were interviewed.
zh: 所有这些青少年都接受了访谈。

en: They were given medical exams.
zh: 他们还接受了身体检查。

en: We went to their homes and we interviewed their parents.
zh: 我们去他们家里，并采访了他们的父母。

en: And then these teenagers grew up into adults
zh: 后来，这些青少年长大成人，

en: who entered all walks of life.
zh: 进入了社会的各行各业。

en: They became factory workers and lawyers and bricklayers and doctors,
zh: 他们有的成为工厂工人、律师、砌砖工或医生，

en: one President of the United States.
zh: 其中一人还成为了美国总统。

en: Some developed alcoholism. A few developed schizophrenia.
zh: 有些人染上了酒瘾，少数人患上了精神分裂症。

en: Some climbed the social ladder
zh: 有些人沿着社会阶梯一路向上，

en: from the bottom all the way to the very top,
zh: 从最底层一直爬到了最顶层，

en: and some made that journey in the opposite direction.
zh: 也有些人走上了完全相反的道路。

en: The founders of this study
zh: 这项研究的创始人

en: would never in their wildest dreams
zh: 即便在最大胆的想象中，

en: have imagined that I would be standing here today, 75 years later,
zh: 也不会想到，75年后的今天，我会站在这里，

en: telling you that the study still continues.
zh: 告诉大家这项研究仍在继续。

en: Every two years, our patient and dedicated research staff
zh: 每隔两年，我们耐心而敬业的研究人员

en: calls up our men and asks them if we can send them
zh: 都会给这些男性打电话，询问是否可以再给他们寄去

en: yet one more set of questions about their lives.
zh: 一套关于他们生活的调查问题。

en: Many of the inner city Boston men ask us,
zh: 许多来自Boston市中心贫困社区的男性会问我们：

en: "Why do you keep wanting to study me? My life just isn't that interesting."
zh: “你们为什么总想研究我？我的人生根本没那么有意思。”

en: The Harvard men never ask that question.
zh: 哈佛的那组人从来不会问这个问题。

en: To get the clearest picture of these lives,
zh: 为了尽可能清楚地了解他们的人生，

en: we don't just send them questionnaires.
zh: 我们并不只是给他们寄调查问卷。

en: We interview them in their living rooms.
zh: 我们会坐在他们的客厅里采访他们。

en: We get their medical records from their doctors.
zh: 我们会从他们的医生那里获取病历。

en: We draw their blood, we scan their brains,
zh: 我们会给他们抽血，扫描他们的大脑，

en: we talk to their children.
zh: 还会与他们的子女交谈。

en: We videotape them talking with their wives about their deepest concerns.
zh: 我们会录下他们与妻子谈论内心最深层忧虑的过程。

en: And when, about a decade ago, we finally asked the wives
zh: 大约十年前，我们终于询问这些妻子，

en: if they would join us as members of the study,
zh: 是否愿意也作为研究对象加入我们时，

en: many of the women said, "You know, it's about time."
zh: 许多女性都说：“你们早就该这么做了。”

en: So what have we learned?
zh: 那么，我们究竟学到了什么？

en: What are the lessons that come from the tens of thousands of pages
zh: 我们积累了数以万计页面的资料，

en: of information that we've generated
zh: 从这些资料中得到的经验和启示

en: on these lives?
zh: 究竟是什么？

en: Well, the lessons aren't about wealth or fame or working harder and harder.
zh: 这些启示与财富、名声或拼命工作无关。

en: The clearest message that we get from this 75-year study is this:
zh: 这项持续75年的研究传达出的最明确的信息是：

en: Good relationships keep us happier and healthier. Period.
zh: 良好的人际关系会让我们更幸福、更健康。就是这么简单。

en: We've learned three big lessons about relationships.
zh: 关于人际关系，我们得出了三条重要结论。

en: The first is that social connections are really good for us,
zh: 第一，社会联系确实对我们非常有益，

en: and that loneliness kills.
zh: 而孤独则会致命。

en: It turns out that people who are more socially connected
zh: 事实证明，与他人拥有更多社会联系的人，

en: to family, to friends, to community,
zh: 无论是与家人、朋友还是社区保持联系，

en: are happier, they're physically healthier, and they live longer
zh: 都会更加幸福，身体更加健康，寿命也更长，

en: than people who are less well connected.
zh: 相比那些社会联系较少的人而言。

en: And the experience of loneliness turns out to be toxic.
zh: 事实还证明，孤独是一种有害的体验。

en: People who are more isolated than they want to be from others
zh: 那些与他人之间的隔绝程度超过自己意愿的人，

en: find that they are less happy,
zh: 往往会感到更加不幸福，

en: their health declines earlier in midlife,
zh: 他们的健康状况会在中年时期更早恶化，

en: their brain functioning declines sooner
zh: 大脑功能也会更早衰退，

en: and they live shorter lives than people who are not lonely.
zh: 寿命也比不孤独的人更短。

en: And the sad fact is that at any given time,
zh: 而一个令人难过的事实是，在任何一个时间点，

en: more than one in five Americans will report that they're lonely.
zh: 超过五分之一的美国人都会表示自己感到孤独。

en: And we know that you can be lonely in a crowd
zh: 我们也知道，即使身处人群之中，你仍然可能感到孤独，

en: and you can be lonely in a marriage,
zh: 即使身处婚姻之中，你也可能感到孤独。

en: so the second big lesson that we learned
zh: 因此，我们得出的第二条重要结论

en: is that it's not just the number of friends you have,
zh: 是关键并不只是你有多少朋友，

en: and it's not whether or not you're in a committed relationship,
zh: 也不在于你是否处于一段稳定的亲密关系中，

en: but it's the quality of your close relationships that matters.
zh: 真正重要的是亲密关系的质量。

en: It turns out that living in the midst of conflict is really bad for our health.
zh: 事实证明，长期生活在冲突之中对健康非常不利。

en: High-conflict marriages, for example, without much affection,
zh: 例如，冲突频繁而又缺乏感情的婚姻，

en: turn out to be very bad for our health, perhaps worse than getting divorced.
zh: 会严重损害健康，甚至可能比离婚更糟。

en: And living in the midst of good, warm relationships is protective.
zh: 而生活在良好、温暖的关系中，则能给我们带来保护。

en: Once we had followed our men all the way into their 80s,
zh: 在我们一路追踪这些男性，直到他们八十多岁之后，

en: we wanted to look back at them at midlife
zh: 我们希望回过头去看看他们的中年时期，

en: and to see if we could predict
zh: 看看我们能否预测，

en: who was going to grow into a happy, healthy octogenarian
zh: 哪些人会成长为幸福、健康的八旬老人，

en: and who wasn't.
zh: 哪些人不会。

en: And when we gathered together everything we knew about them
zh: 当我们汇总了自己掌握的关于他们的一切信息，

en: at age 50,
zh: 也就是他们50岁时的所有资料后，

en: it wasn't their middle age cholesterol levels
zh: 能够预测他们将如何老去的，

en: that predicted how they were going to grow old.
zh: 并不是他们中年时期的胆固醇水平。

en: It was how satisfied they were in their relationships.
zh: 而是他们对自己的人际关系有多满意。

en: The people who were the most satisfied in their relationships at age 50
zh: 那些在50岁时对人际关系最满意的人，

en: were the healthiest at age 80.
zh: 到了80岁时身体也最健康。

en: And good, close relationships seem to buffer us
zh: 良好而亲密的关系似乎还能帮助我们抵御

en: from some of the slings and arrows of getting old.
zh: 衰老过程中遭遇的一些痛苦与打击。

en: Our most happily partnered men and women
zh: 在伴侣关系中最幸福的男性和女性，

en: reported, in their 80s,
zh: 在八十多岁时表示，

en: that on the days when they had more physical pain,
zh: 即使某一天身体上的疼痛更加强烈，

en: their mood stayed just as happy.
zh: 他们的情绪依然能保持同样愉快。

en: But the people who were in unhappy relationships,
zh: 但那些身处不幸福关系中的人，

en: on the days when they reported more physical pain,
zh: 在身体疼痛更加强烈的日子里，

en: it was magnified by more emotional pain.
zh: 这种疼痛还会因情感上的痛苦而进一步加剧。

en: And the third big lesson that we learned about relationships and our health
zh: 关于人际关系与健康，我们得到的第三条重要结论

en: is that good relationships don't just protect our bodies,
zh: 是良好的人际关系不仅能保护我们的身体，

en: they protect our brains.
zh: 也能保护我们的大脑。

en: It turns out that being in a securely attached relationship
zh: 事实证明，到了八十多岁时，拥有一段安全可靠的亲密关系，

en: to another person in your 80s is protective,
zh: 能够对人产生保护作用。

en: that the people who are in relationships
zh: 那些身处一段关系中，

en: where they really feel they can count on the other person in times of need,
zh: 并真心觉得自己在需要帮助时可以依靠对方的人，

en: those people's memories stay sharper longer.
zh: 他们的记忆力能够更长久地保持敏锐。

en: And the people in relationships
zh: 而那些身处一段关系中，

en: where they feel they really can't count on the other one,
zh: 却觉得自己根本无法依靠对方的人，

en: those are the people who experience earlier memory decline.
zh: 往往会更早出现记忆力衰退。

en: And those good relationships, they don't have to be smooth all the time.
zh: 而且，良好的人际关系并不意味着永远都要和和睦睦。

en: Some of our octogenarian couples could bicker with each other
zh: 我们研究中的一些八旬夫妻也会彼此争吵，

en: day in and day out,
zh: 甚至天天拌嘴，

en: but as long as they felt that they could really count on the other
zh: 但只要他们觉得，在真正遇到困难时，

en: when the going got tough,
zh: 自己确实可以依靠对方，

en: those arguments didn't take a toll on their memories.
zh: 这些争吵就不会损害他们的记忆力。

en: So this message,
zh: 所以，这条信息，

en: that good, close relationships are good for our health and well-being,
zh: 也就是良好而亲密的关系有益于我们的健康与幸福，

en: this is wisdom that's as old as the hills.
zh: 其实是一条古老得不能再古老的智慧。

en: Why is this so hard to get and so easy to ignore?
zh: 那为什么我们如此难以真正理解它，却又如此容易忽视它？

en: Well, we're human.
zh: 因为我们终究是人。

en: What we'd really like is a quick fix,
zh: 我们真正想要的是一种立竿见影的解决办法，

en: something we can get
zh: 一种能够轻松获得的东西，

en: that'll make our lives good and keep them that way.
zh: 让我们的人生变得美好，并永远保持下去。

en: Relationships are messy and they're complicated
zh: 人际关系混乱而复杂，

en: and the hard work of tending to family and friends,
zh: 而用心维系家人和朋友之间的关系，

en: it's not sexy or glamorous.
zh: 既不性感，也不光鲜亮丽。

en: It's also lifelong. It never ends.
zh: 而且这是一辈子的事，永远没有终点。

en: The people in our 75-year study who were the happiest in retirement
zh: 在这项持续75年的研究中，退休后最幸福的人，

en: were the people who had actively worked to replace workmates with new playmates.
zh: 都是那些主动结交新玩伴，以取代昔日同事的人。

en: Just like the millennials in that recent survey,
zh: 就像最近那项调查中的千禧一代一样，

en: many of our men when they were starting out as young adults
zh: 我们的许多研究对象在刚步入成年时，

en: really believed that fame and wealth and high achievement
zh: 也深信名声、财富和卓越成就

en: were what they needed to go after to have a good life.
zh: 才是过上美好人生所必须追求的东西。

en: But over and over, over these 75 years, our study has shown
zh: 但在这75年里，我们的研究一次又一次地表明，

en: that the people who fared the best were the people who leaned in to relationships,
zh: 生活得最好的人，是那些积极投入人际关系的人，

en: with family, with friends, with community.
zh: 投入与家人、朋友和社区的关系。

en: So what about you?
zh: 那么你呢？

en: Let's say you're 25, or you're 40, or you're 60.
zh: 假设你现在25岁、40岁或60岁。

en: What might leaning in to relationships even look like?
zh: 积极投入人际关系，具体可以是什么样子？

en: Well, the possibilities are practically endless.
zh: 其实可以采取的方式几乎无穷无尽。

en: It might be something as simple as replacing screen time with people time
zh: 它可能只是把看屏幕的时间换成与人相处的时间，

en: or livening up a stale relationship by doing something new together,
zh: 或者和对方一起尝试新鲜事物，为一段乏味的关系重新注入活力，

en: long walks or date nights,
zh: 比如一起散步，或者安排约会之夜，

en: or reaching out to that family member who you haven't spoken to in years,
zh: 又或者主动联系那个已经多年没有说过话的家人，

en: because those all-too-common family feuds
zh: 因为那些再常见不过的家庭矛盾，

en: take a terrible toll
zh: 会给人带来沉重的伤害，

en: on the people who hold the grudges.
zh: 尤其是那些始终心怀怨恨的人。

en: I'd like to close with a quote from Mark Twain.
zh: 最后，我想引用Mark Twain的一句话来结束今天的演讲。

en: More than a century ago,
zh: 一个多世纪以前，

en: he was looking back on his life,
zh: 他回顾自己的一生，

en: and he wrote this:
zh: 写下了这样一段话：

en: "There isn't time, so brief is life,
zh: “人生如此短暂，我们没有时间

en: for bickerings, apologies, heartburnings, callings to account.
zh: 去争吵、道歉、心怀怨恨或追究责任。

en: There is only time for loving,
zh: 我们只有时间去爱，

en: and but an instant, so to speak, for that."
zh: 而严格来说，就连用来爱的时间也不过短短一瞬。”

en: The good life is built with good relationships.
zh: 美好的人生，由良好的人际关系构筑而成。

en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢大家。
